transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been getting pulled off task really easily. For about the past year, even small things—a phone buzz, someone walking by my office, or just some random thought—can derail me before I really catch it.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Yeah… somewhat. If I’m supposed to sit still, like at a family dinner or one of the volunteer meetings at church, I get this feeling like I need to move. Like there’s a motor running inside, I guess. I’ll mess with my hands or look for something to do.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Sometimes, yeah. It’s more like… I’ll cut in before I think about it. I’ve jumped into my wife’s conversations with her parents, or finished an employee’s thought before they’re done. I can tell it annoys people.
Have you had difficulty completing tasks or assignments at work or school?

Yeah, at work mostly. I can start a planning document or sit down with one of my managers and feel like I’m following at first, but then a few minutes later I realize I missed a lot of what was said. I’ll have to ask them to go back over it.
Do you often feel the need to be on the go or run around, even when you're not supposed to be doing anything physically active?

Yeah… I guess so. Not running around exactly, but when I’m supposed to just sit, like at dinner or a church meeting, I feel like I need to move or do something with my hands. Like I can’t really just be still.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?
Yeah… I do. I’ll cut people off without meaning to. Like with my wife’s conversations, or at work I’ll finish someone’s thought before they’re done. I can tell it doesn’t always land well.
Were you more physically active or restless than your peers when you were a child?
Yeah, I think so. Looking back, teachers were always moving my seat around because I’d talk too much, get up without asking, or blurt something out before they were even done asking.
Did you have difficulty following rules or waiting for your turn as a child?
Yeah… I mean, I think so. Teachers were always moving my seat because I’d talk too much or get up without asking. I’d blurt out answers before they were even done with the question sometimes.
Did you have trouble paying attention in class when you were a kid?
Yeah, some. I’d be listening at first, but after a few minutes I’d sort of realize I’d missed part of what the teacher was saying. I still do that now in meetings sometimes.
Were you often described as overly energetic or hyperactive as a child?

Yeah, I guess so. I don’t know if people used that exact word, but looking back, as a kid teachers were always moving my seat because I’d talk too much, get up without asking, or blurt things out before they finished the question.
Did you often get in trouble for not following instructions as a kid?
Yeah… I got in trouble some. Mostly teachers moving my seat because I was talking too much, getting up when I wasn’t supposed to, or answering before they finished asking.
Have you experienced these symptoms of inattention and impulsivity your entire life, or did they start at some point?

I think it’s pretty much always been there. Looking back, it was definitely around when I was a kid—teachers moving my seat because I talked too much, got up without asking, or blurted stuff out before they even finished.
Have these symptoms caused you any problems at work or in your relationships with others?

Yeah… some. I mean, I’m still keeping up overall, but it does cause friction. At work people can get impatient with me in meetings or when I’m supposed to be mentoring someone and it doesn’t go smoothly. And at home… it’s started to affect trust a bit when family plans don’t go the way they’re supposed to.
Have you experienced significant periods in your life where these symptoms were not a problem?
Not really. It’s been around, but it’s been harder to manage for maybe… a little over a year now. Since the issues with my in-laws started taking up more of our family life, I guess.
Have these symptoms caused you significant distress?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m falling apart or anything. I’m still keeping up overall. But it does bother me that people at work lose patience with me, and at home it’s… starting to affect trust when plans don’t go the way they should. So, yeah, some distress.
Do you often feel excessively fidgety or restless when you're sitting still as an adult?

Yeah… I do. If I’m supposed to just sit still, like at a family dinner or a church meeting, I get this… kind of motor-running feeling. I usually need to shift around or mess with something in my hands.
Have these symptoms ever caused you to lose a job, damage a significant relationship, or significantly impair your ability to function in daily life?

I haven’t lost a job or anything like that. I’m still functioning, mostly. But it has started to affect things… like people at work getting impatient when meetings or mentoring conversations don’t go smoothly, and at home when family plans fall through, it costs me some trust.
Have you ever felt like these symptoms have significantly held you back from achieving your goals or reaching your full potential at work or in your personal life?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still keeping up overall, so I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. But it does feel like it’s starting to cost me… people’s patience at work, and some trust at home when plans or conversations don’t go how they should.
Have you ever had a period of at least a few months where you didn't experience any of these symptoms?

Not really, no. It’s been harder to manage for… about a year and a couple months now, since the in-law conflict started taking over more of our family life. Before that I guess it was there, but not as noticeable.
Have these symptoms ever caused you to have significant problems with your daily life, such as being unable to take care of things at home or having trouble doing your job?

I’m not unable to handle things, no. I’m still keeping up overall. But… yeah, it’s starting to cause problems. At work, people get impatient when meetings or mentoring conversations don’t go well, and at home, when family plans fall through, it chips away at trust a bit.
